newsitem.title: JAPAN: Price increase not yet a worry in Japan - EPA.
newsitem.headline: Price increase not yet a worry in Japan - EPA.

text.p: Japan does not have to worry yet about inflationary pressures from the yen's weakness against the dollar, which is pushing up prices of imported goods, Economic Planning Agency (EPA) Vice Minister Shimpei Nukaya said on Tuesday.
"It is true that the prices of imported goods are rising. But the situation is not one that we must be worried about," he said.
He said there were no signs that higher import prices were pushing up overall prices in Japan.
He said the yen's fall against the dollar was due to a number of factors, such as low domestic interest rates, a decline in Japan's trade surplus and the strength of each countries' economy.
"It is not necessary to think that the situation (in the currency market) is removed from economic fundamentals," Nukaya said at the Foreign Correspondents Club of Japan.
